title: kv-cache-adaptive-compaction-spillover-eviction-policy-improvements
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and frequent spillover to host memory under variable sequence-length workloads is increasing tail latency and useful cache hit rates. This PR introduces an adaptive compaction and eviction policy that reduces fragmentation, improves paging decisions, and lowers spillover-induced latency spikes. Approach: 1) introduce an in-memory compaction pass that runs opportunistically when fragmentation exceeds a heuristically-tuned threshold, 2) add an age-and-cost eviction priority that favors evicting low-value entries which contribute most to fragmentation, 3) implement a paging budget that limits async spillover throughput to host memory under load to avoid IO backpressure cascading into scheduling stalls, 4) expose two tunables via kv-cache config (compaction_threshold_pct, paging_budget_ms_per_sec) and a telemetry hook for fragmentation metrics. Implementation notes: compaction is incremental and lock-free from the hot path by using slot-ownership handoffs and a light-weight relocation table; eviction priority uses per-shard recency + fragment_cost score computed from entry size delta and adjacency; paging budget uses per-device token-clock accounting and defers non-critical spill operations. Compatibility: fallback to previous eviction logic if compaction fails or if running on legacy kernels. Testing: unit tests for eviction priority, integration tests with synthetic batching workloads, performance benchmark harness runs showing 12-28% reduction in p99 token latency on mixed short/long sequence traces and 9-15% improvement in useful cache hit rate on production-derived traces. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked ENG-2147 - [x] unit and integration tests added - [x] e2e perf run attached - [x] telemetry metrics and dashboards updated - [x] config knobs documented Rollout plan: staged rollout via canary pool then gradual ramp over 2 weeks; automatic rollback if p99 latency regression > 10% for 5m. Backwards compatibility and migration: no model or customer-visible schema changes; default knobs preserve legacy behaviour until enabled in configuration. Risks and mitigations: compaction may introduce transient CPU overhead; mitigated via adaptive throttling and rate limiter; paging budget mis-config may increase memory pressure, mitigated by conservative defaults and runtime safety checks. Referenced artifacts: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2147/kv-cache-adaptive-compaction and perf runs in /bench/kv-cache/2026-01-28. Summary: shipping this improves tail latency and cache usefulness while providing controls for operators to tune trade-offs across hardware families.
commits: fix: initial adaptive compaction algorithm and relocation table implementation
feat: add eviction priority scoring (recency + fragment_cost)

test: unit tests for eviction priority and compactor
docs: kv-cache config knobs and rollout notes

review_comments: Marco Ruiz (2026-01-20): Can you clarify the lock-free guarantees for the relocation table? The design doc mentions handoffs but code looks to take a brief atomic swap in a few hot paths.

Priya Nair (2026-01-20): The relocation table uses atomic pointer swaps per-slot; the hot path only does a single atomic compare-and-swap to claim a slot, compaction performs multi-slot moves off the hot path. Added an inline comment and a small microbenchmark to the tests to validate the CAS count.
Aisha Khan (2026-01-22): The paging_budget unit is ms_per_sec which is odd to operators, can we expose it as percentage of IO budget to be consistent with other runtime knobs?
Priya Nair (2026-01-22): Agreed, added an alias 'paging_budget_pct_io' and kept ms_per_sec for backwards compatibility. Updated docs and example config.
Ben Thompson (2026-01-24): I saw a 3% p50 regression in one canary run; is that from compaction CPU overhead?

Priya Nair (2026-01-24): Investigated the run; regression correlated with compaction enabled on small instance types. Added adaptive throttling tied to CPU headroom and disabled compaction by default on smaller instance classes. Canary re-run shows the regression gone and improved p99.
Marco Ruiz (2026-01-28): Tests look good. One last nit: prefer kFragmentationThreshold over magic literal in component ctor.
Priya Nair (2026-01-28): Addressed, replaced literals with named constants and added a unit test that verifies threshold behavior.
Aisha Khan (2026-01-29): Approved after docs update.
CI Bot (2026-02-01): All checks passed on CI. Performance harness reported 15% p99 improvement in mixed-trace-run-2026-01-28.
Release Manager (2026-02-01): Merging to main via squash after smoke-run.
release_notes: Adaptive KV cache compaction and eviction improvements that reduce fragmentation and spillover-induced tail latency. New knobs: compaction_threshold_pct, paging_budget_ms_per_sec (alias paging_budget_pct_io). Improves p99 latency and cache hit rate for mixed short/long workloads. Rollout via canary with automatic rollback on regression.
notes: Operators should monitor kv_cache.fragmentation_pct, kv_cache.spill_io_ms, and p99_token_latency during rollout. Default behavior preserves legacy eviction until compaction enabled via config.
